description: Main window: open/save dialogs, read only files the user chose, and the settings store. The page writes no file itself: saves go through the app's own commands below, which check the fs scope. The fs permissions carry no static scope: the dialog plugin adds each picked or saved file at runtime, and the fs plugin adds dropped paths. A dropped folder (which the app never opens) is added recursively for the rest of the session; that is the fs plugin's built-in drop rule, and turning it off would also stop dropped files from opening. window:allow-destroy closes the window after the unsaved-changes prompt; window:allow-show shows the window, which starts hidden, once the page has drawn its first frame. The allow-<command> entries grant the app's own commands (overwrite-with-backup and save-copy saves, both written through a temporary file and a rename, the saved-review session commands, and the writing helper's sha256-file, llm-start, llm-stop and llm-installed (whether the helper's files are there; it reads nothing else): Rust starts the bundled llama-server with a fixed argument list, so there is no shell permission; and os-locale, the Windows regional format that picks the fallback English variant, as the CLI's Node does); build.rs declares them in the app manifest, so no other command is callable. The scoped fs:allow-read-file entry lets the app read one bundled file, the word-lookup dictionary ($RESOURCE/dictionary/oewn.json.gz, read-only: no write permission is scoped to it).
